clue.text: Posh bloke is a Tory bastard? Not unknown

indicators.note: used as an adjective, bastard means corrupt or debased, so the letters of is a Tory are rearranged
Not here says the following letter is to be left out of the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, x, y and z

explanation.surface: A jibe at an upper-class man as a no-good Conservative, with a pseudo-mathematical aside tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y away from the letters of IS A TORY and ISATOR remains; 'bastard' shuffles those six letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is informal shorthand for an aristocrat, the classic posh bloke.

clue.text: Rare element of sexual excitement with female — I'm keeping out, essentially

parts.note: rut is the season of sexual excitement in deer and other animals
a hen is a female bird, and loosely any female

indicators.note: keeping means the letters of I'm hold the next piece within them

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or central letter of the word out

parts.note: U is the middle letter of out

explanation.surface: A racy confession about excitement with a woman while the speaker stays away, dressed up as chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: RUT and HEN come first; then IM keeps U, the heart of 'out', giving IUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthenium is a rare metallic element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Soldiers arrested by police officers around base

indicators.note: soldiers arrested by police are held inside them
around tells us to turn the officers' letters back to front

parts.note: DI and DS are detective inspector and detective sergeant
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A news story about troops detained by the police somewhere near a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: DI + DS reversed gives SDID, and OR is held within it. 'base' looks like a military camp but is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the moral sense means low or contemptible, just as something sordid is ignoble and squalid.

clue.text: Getting on coach is traditional

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old
to coach is to train or school someone

explanation.surface: Boarding a bus or carriage is the time-honoured way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' reads as a vehicle but is the verb meaning train.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes conservative, conventional ways of doing things, as traditional does.

clue.text: Usual performance quietly meets with approval

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a tick is a mark of approval

explanation.surface: A performer's regular act, delivered softly, wins applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a comedian's or entertainer's familiar routine or gimmick.

clue.text: Child's yellow — doctors gathering round

indicators.note: round tells us to turn the whole assembly of doctors and colour about
the doctors gather the colour in, holding it inside

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Doctors cluster around a jaundiced child.
explanation.walkthrough: GPS gathers OR to make GORPS, and 'round' turns that about. In 'Child's', the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child, especially a baby.

clue.text: Roars during day end squabbling

indicators.note: during means the next part goes inside the day's letters

parts.note: Thurs is the abbreviation for Thursday

indicators.note: squabbling suggests the letters of end are at odds and jumbled

explanation.surface: Shouting breaks out as a day ends in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' looks like the close of the day in the surface, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To thunder is to make a loud deep noise or shout angrily, much like roaring.

clue.text: Desperately want to be in Conservative Party?

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone longs to join the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' is a link here; the question mark flags the political-party misreading of 'Party'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is to long for something with intense desire.

clue.text: Changed key before end of ballad

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of ballad

parts.note: D is the last letter of ballad

explanation.surface: A song that shifted key just before its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests music, but it is the keyboard key ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered means modified or made different, a direct synonym of changed.

clue.text: Makes an enemy of worker and worries deeply

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
to agonise is to worry intensely

explanation.surface: An employee who frets so much they turn into an adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to provoke hostility, turning them into a foe.

clue.text: Plant roses at front except in centre

indicators.note: at front selects the first letter of roses

parts.note: R is the first letter of roses

indicators.note: in places the next piece inside the centre's letters

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity
bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: put roses at the front of a bed but not in its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' reads as a link in the surface, but it is a synonym in its own right, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a garden plant grown for its edible pink stalks.

clue.text: Dirty resort has improved on the surface

indicators.note: the improved word wraps around the resort, lying on its surface on both sides

parts.note: bettered means improved
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A seaside town has smartened up, but only superficially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is the piece held inside; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespattered means splashed with mud or stains, so soiled.

clue.text: Big Tech (and Ted's dosh) could possibly bring material success

indicators.note: could possibly hints that the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Tech giants, and someone called Ted's cash, might bring riches.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of BIG TECH and TEDS DOSH rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitch-goddess is William James's phrase for worldly success, the idol of material wealth.

clue.text: Good book plausible on the surface

parts.note: lib is short for liber, Latin for book, as in lib. on library shelves

explanation.surface: A worthwhile read that only seems convincing at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib speech is smooth and fluent but shallow, persuasive without substance.

clue.text: Sure to make a move after trick one's played

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled piece behind the trick

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: to make a move tells us one letter of the synonym for sure shifts its position

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A chess or card player confidently moves after a ruse is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's played' means a thing that is played, an instrument, not a move in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small squeezebox, a musical instrument someone plays.

clue.text: See something useful in the kitchen

parts.note: See sounds like the letter C, which is the opener, or first letter, of the word can

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a handy kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'See' as the letter C: it opens the word CAN, so it is a can's opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-opener is a kitchen gadget for cutting open tins.

clue.text: Bothered by independence, right — judged it to be divisive

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

indicators.note: it divides the judged word by sitting inside it

parts.note: rated means judged or assessed

explanation.surface: Someone upset by a political split over independence and the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divisive' looks political, but here it means the little word divides the longer one.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated means annoyed, which is what bothered means here.

clue.text: Advice about protecting endlessly vulnerable — it's a nasty place

indicators.note: the reversed word surrounds and protects the next piece
about tells us to turn the advice word around

parts.note: tips are pieces of advice

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: naked means exposed or vulnerable

explanation.surface: Advice for shielding the defenceless from somewhere unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: TIPS reversed is SPIT; NAKED loses its end to give NAKE, which SPIT protects.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake pit is figuratively a place of chaos or viciousness, literally a pit of serpents.

clue.text: Invaders ignoring rule left with ground unclaimed

indicators.note: ignoring means the rule letter is left out

parts.note: the Normans invaded England in 1066
R is the abbreviation for rule, as in rex or regina's rule
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Invaders who break the rules take land nobody owns.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMANS without R is NOMANS, then L and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: No-man's-land is territory between front lines that neither side holds.

clue.text: Idiot holding back star pupil? On the contrary

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read in reverse
holding means the answer sits inside the words that follow
on the contrary reverses the clue's claim: the star pupil holds the idiot, not the other way round

explanation.surface: A fool keeps the top student behind, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned around, the clue says 'star pupil' holds the idiot backwards: sTAR Pupil gives TARP, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a foolish or incompetent person.

clue.text: Polluted river in which crew's emptied effluents

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of effluents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: E and S are the outer letters of effluents

explanation.surface: A dirty river into which a gang has dumped waste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is India's great sacred river, notoriously contaminated by sewage.

clue.text: Steal script craftily when Charles is inside dressing

indicators.note: is inside places the king within the shuffled letters
craftily suggests the letters are slyly rearranged

parts.note: Charles III is King

explanation.surface: A cunning plan to steal a manuscript while the King is indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles is the current British monarch, so he gives KING; 'dressing' is a wound dressing, not clothing or salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is an adhesive dressing for a small wound.

clue.text: Dancing ladies beginning to strip off — this couldn't be better

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of ladies move about
off says the following letter is removed from the fodder
beginning to picks the first letter of strip

parts.note: S is the first letter of strip

explanation.surface: Women dancing, starting to undress, in a scene someone thinks perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: LADIES without the S from 'strip' leaves LADIE, which rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something perfect, which nothing could improve on.

clue.text: Square up over drinker's last bottle

indicators.note: over means the reversed word covers the next letter, around it
in a down clue, up means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to be square is to be even, all debts settled

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of drinker's

parts.note: R is the last letter of drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker settles the bill before finishing the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN reversed is NEVE, which goes over R to give the answer. 'bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and bottle both mean courage or daring.

clue.text: Doubly small for a defender

parts.note: small twice: S, the abbreviation, then wee, Scots for small
per means for, as in per head

explanation.surface: A tiny defender, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a sweeper is the defender who plays behind the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is a defensive player in football who covers behind the other defenders.

clue.text: Want to carry gun but denied

indicators.note: to carry means the want word holds the gun inside it

parts.note: need means want or lack
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone wished to bear arms but was refused.
explanation.walkthrough: Gat is old American gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or nullify, so negated means denied.

clue.text: Chance to wear revolutionary dress

indicators.note: to wear means the revolutionary has the chance word on him, around it

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
lot means chance, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: An opportunity to put on rebel clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is a noun here, the Argentine guerrilla Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to dress them, provide garments.

clue.text: Stay on team

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a side is a team

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay on team' reads as remaining in a squad, but it splits into a definition and a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or live somewhere, a sense of staying.
